About Event

Spatial Intelligence + Generative 3D Hackathon — Event Plan
World Labs × Tripo × mint.gg × Convex.dev · One-day hackathon · San Francisco
Overview
We're teaming up with World Labs , Tripo , mint.gg , and Convex.dev for a one-day hackathon in San Francisco at the intersection of spatial intelligence and generative 3D.
Participants will get hands-on access to some of the best tools for generating 3D content and turning it into functional, interactive experiences:
World Labs — large world models for generating immersive worlds

Tripo — rapid 3D asset generation for creating game-ready objects

mint.gg — agentic creation platform and developer tools for bringing worlds and assets together as interactive, playable experiences

Convex.dev — real-time backend infrastructure for powering application data, state, multiplayer systems, and agentic experiences

Together, we'll explore what becomes possible when entire worlds, detailed 3D objects, and real-time scenes can be generated from little more than a prompt or an image — and then quickly assembled, programmed, connected, and shared.
Tracks
Gaming & Interactive Worlds — Playable worlds, games, multiplayer experiences, interactive applications, and real-time 3D scenes

Physical AI & Simulation — Robotics, simulation, embodied agents, spatial reasoning, training environments, and digital twins

Creative 3D & VFX — Visual effects, virtual production, cinematic experiences, creative tools, real-time graphics, and experimental projects that do not fit neatly into the other tracks

The top two teams in each of the three tracks will each receive:
$1k in World Labs credits

About Event

Agents are already using your product. They are just doing it by pretending to be a human.
Spend two days at Cloudflare SF building and hacking a version of your product that is ready for agents. Not one agent. A fleet of them: agents that discover each other, hand work off, and finish a job together without a human relaying between them. In the room we will have industry leading agent native developers that will be assisting you with your projects.
Limited to 50 builder seats reserved for August 26 and 27 at Cloudflare HQ in San Francisco.
This is a one of a kind agentic hackathon, where we are selecting startups to participate and upgrade their tech.
Once selected, we will be coordinating, co-building and submitting your projects through your terminal agents.
You'll join the immersivecommons platform, currently ranked #1 on ora.ai and scoring a 100/100 on isitagentready.com . where our sponsoring entities will provide forward deployed agents to help you with your projects on this platform, including credits and other forms of help!
Hosted by Immersive Commons , Runtype and Cotal.ai .
What you are building
Whether its a customer facing product or an internal company tooling, in this hackathon make your existing platforms agent ready! Ready for one agent is table stakes. The interesting work starts when several show up at once and have to coordinate.
Things we care about most:
Discovery: Is your platform and services discoverable by other agents

Access: Does your platform allow agents to access your services securely

Usability: How easy is it for people with their agents to access your product

Payments: Can agents make payments on your platform.

Accessibility: How easy it is for humans on your platform access AI tooling without having/owning AI.

Pick a track
EXTERNAL - Customer facing: Build/deploy meaningful agent infrastructure to an existing product/platform using one or more of our partner companies. The customer's agent does not arrive alone. Assume it brings its own fleet and has to negotiate with yours.
INTERNAL - Team facing: Build/deploy meaningful agent infrastructure for internal company use using one or more of our partner companies. This is where orchestration lives: your agents running your workflows across teams and systems that were never built to talk to each other.
Who is in the room
50 builders from startups that have already shipped. We hope to see shippable demos by the end.
Getting in
Registering on this page tells us you are interested. It does not hold a seat.
If candidate selected, we will message you to join the platform.
Your agent can fill it out for you through our MCP server, which is the most on brand thing you could possibly do.
Applications close soon.
Badges print from legal names. Apply with the name on your ID, not your handle.

Doors 9:00 AM, building clears 8:00 PM, both days. There is no overnight.

Awards: six winners, three in each track.
Runtype: $500 cash for the best use of Runtype.

Tavily: 8,000 credits for every builder.

Runtype: $50 in credits for every builder.

Nebius: credits, amount to be confirmed.

Hacker Bob: credits, amount to be confirmed.

Address: Cloudflare SF, 101 Townsend Street.
Who is behind this
Cloudflare gives us the room at 101 Townsend, an employee on site for both days, printed badges and the venue NDA. They host us. They are not a sponsor and they are not paying for anything, which is worth saying plainly because most collateral in this space blurs the two.
Organised by
Immersive Commons ( immersivecommons.com ) is a members run AI builder floor at Frontier Tower SF, 300+ members deep, home of Vibe Coding Nights and the Web for Agents series. The platform itself is agent native end to end, so it is also the worked example you build against.
Runtype ( runtype.com ) is a product platform for agentic software. Agents, flows, tools, product evals, model routing and integrations already wired together, so a prompt that works becomes a product without you rebuilding auth, multi tenancy and evals first.
Cotal.ai ( cotal.ai ) is an open coordination standard for fleets of agents, Apache 2.0 and self hosted. Identity the server verifies instead of the agent asserting, default deny access lists, and one ordered replayable log of every message, so a handoff is auditable rather than hopeful.
Sponsors
Tenki ( tenki.cloud ) is cloud infrastructure for code and agents. Disposable Linux sandboxes that boot in under two seconds and bill by the second, drop in CI runners, and AI code review on every pull request. Their startup program is live at up to $50K in credits and grants.
Nebius ( nebius.com ) is a GPU cloud engineered from silicon to API. Bare metal GPUs on InfiniBand, clusters in minutes, managed and serverless inference on top. For when the model you need will not run on a laptop.
Tavily ( tavily.com ) is the web access layer for agents. Search, extract, crawl and map behind one API, returning clean chunked content, with PII and prompt injection filtering in front of it. 2M+ developers, ranked first on SealQA and SimpleQA.
Mitosis Labs ( mitosislabs.ai ) is the source of truth your agents read from. Memory that survives the session, first on the public accuracy benchmark at 91.7%, every answer citing where it came from, in about half a second.
Hacker Bob ( hackerbob.ai ) is an Apache 2.0 security testing runtime shipped as an MCP server, with 17 assigned CVE IDs across 9 open source projects. Point it at the surface you just opened to agents.
Community partners
Agent Community ( agentcommunity.org ) is the open community building the agentic web, 29,000+ members across 8,000+ organizations, with public work streams on identity, security, evaluations, trust and governance.
Learning Layer Labs ( learninglayer.ai ) builds events and labs at the frontier of AI, education, arts, robotics. Branches in San Francisco and Mexico City, two more coming. They run the AI Floor at Frontier Tower and the labs that turn the room's ideas into shipped work.
ClawCamp ( clawcamp.org ) is a nonprofit advancing mastery of personal AI agents, 16 chapters and 28 events so far, from San Francisco to Nairobi to Zanzibar.
Dabl Club ( dablclub.com ) is a developer relations and go to market community of 83,000+ builders, with local chapters across 20+ countries.
Web A ( weba.network ) is the movement this hackathon belongs to: version zero of the web, built for agents. We are at A.0 and building to A.1.
HiRey ( hirey.ai ) is the IRL social network for people who connect people. Real meetings become claimable pages and a trusted people network that agents can read without a login wall, so who you met here does not evaporate on Friday.
Every one of them is in the room or in the stack. Pick a track, pick the partners you build on, and use the people who wrote the thing.

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.
More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is organized in collaboration with Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) and FLEETWERX.
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

About Event

You get an agent working in an afternoon. Then you point it at something that matters and it can't reach your tools, can't run its own code safely, and can't be stopped before it does damage. Spend a day building one that can do all three.
🧑‍💻 What you are building
A working AI agent, in a day. Pick a job worth handing to an agent, in any field you like, and build the agent that does it. Devtools, operations, data, consumer apps, multi-agent systems: the domain is yours.
A chatbot answers questions. An agent acts on them: it opens the pull request, queries the database, runs the script, sends the message. That is the bar. Bring an idea or pick one up when you arrive, then present your project live to the judges at the end of the day.
🛠️ The tools
You will build on an open-source agent harness , introduced in the morning workshops. A harness is the layer between a model and everything it acts on. It runs the loop your agent works in, sending the model its instructions, calling the tools it asks for, feeding results back, and keeping context and session state across turns. Practically, that means you get:
Connections to your tools. Any MCP server, including ones behind OAuth, plus built-in tools and web search.

Sandboxed execution. Agent-written code runs somewhere isolated.

Human approvals. Pause before sensitive actions until a person signs off.

Subagents. Delegate parts of a job to other agents.

Sessions that survive reconnects. A run keeps going through a refresh or a restart.

Any model provider. OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Skip the plumbing and spend the day on the agent itself.
Qodo is an AI code review platform. Its agents review your pull requests against your full codebase rather than just the diff, flag real bugs and breaking changes ranked by severity, and can apply the fix.
OpenAI is providing $50 in credits to everyone who attends , so you are not paying to experiment.
🏆 Prizes
Best Use of the Agent Harness: NVIDIA DGX Spark Personal AI Supercomputer, worth $5,000. Presented by TrueFoundry . For the agent that gets the most out of the harness. What matters is that the harness is doing the work rather than sitting underneath a thin wrapper.
Best Code Quality: Mac Mini. Presented by Qodo. For the team that treats a hackathon repo like real software. Run your pull requests through Qodo and deal with what it finds before you merge. Using Qodo is required for this track.
Best blog post: Keychron keyboard. Write up what you built, how you wired it together, and what broke along the way. Publish it anywhere.
A team can win one track, not all.
💡 Project ideas
Start from one of these, or bring your own.
Code review agent. Reads a pull request, runs the test suite in a sandbox, and comments on what it found.

Incident responder. Investigates an alert with read-only queries, then asks a person before restarting or rolling anything back.

Analytics agent. Answers questions in plain English by writing the SQL itself, running it, and explaining the result.

Research desk. Sends subagents across the web on a single question and merges what they find, with sources.

Approval-gated assistant. Drafts the email, files the ticket, or books the trip, and does nothing irreversible until you approve it.

Untrusted code runner. Executes code submitted by someone else inside an isolated sandbox and returns the result safely.

Teams of one to four. Free to attend. Come on your own and find people there. Your repo needs to be open source.
Bring a laptop, a charger, and ID for venue entry. Food and Wi-Fi are covered.
Open to platform, infrastructure, and backend engineers, anyone working with LLMs, tool calling, or MCP, founders taking an agent prototype further, and anyone who wants to build their first agent without writing the runtime themselves.

About Event

A 3-day hackathon at Hacker Dojo bringing together veterans, engineers, designers, nonprofit leaders, and community builders to co-create solutions to challenges faced by the veteran community.
The Challenge
What was the hardest part about coming home as a veteran?
For many veterans, the challenge does not end when they leave the service. It begins when they try to navigate the systems designed to support them.
Too often, veterans face:
Confusing websites and complicated processes

Long application forms

Unclear pathways to finding the right resources

Waiting weeks or months for support when they need it most

When a veteran needs help, accessing support should not feel like another battle.
The goal of this hackathon is to explore solutions that make getting support as simple and accessible as possible. We believe veterans should be able to communicate what they need and quickly connect with the right resources, organizations, and people who can help.
Listen First. Then Build.
This hackathon is built around a simple principle:
Listen first, then build.
Veterans will share their lived experiences, challenges, and ideas directly with builders. Engineers, designers, and innovators will then collaborate with veterans to transform those insights into working prototypes over the course of the weekend.
The goal is not just to create a project for a weekend. The goal is to build ideas that can continue growing into real tools, services, and solutions that improve the lives of veterans.

About Event

The Universal Celebration Buildathon is where the entire AI ecosystem comes together.
This isn't just a competition to build projects—it's a celebration of innovation, collaboration, and the people shaping the future of AI. From developers and designers to founders, business owners, marketers, product leaders, researchers, creators, investors, developer advocates, and community builders, everyone has a role to play.
Whether you're building your first AI application, validating a startup idea, exploring how AI can transform your business, designing exceptional user experiences, or simply looking to connect with inspiring people, this event is designed for you.
Come for the hackathon. Leave with new ideas, collaborators, mentors, customers, partners, and opportunities.
🌟 Event Experience
Experience a full day of AI innovation, collaboration, and community.
Participants will build AI-native solutions across innovation tracks while learning from industry experts, engaging with mentors, showcasing live demos, and networking with founders, investors, creators, and ecosystem leaders. Beyond the competition, the event is designed to foster meaningful connections, collaboration, and new opportunities.
👥 Who Should Attend?
The Universal Celebration Hackathon welcomes anyone passionate about innovation with AI.
Whether you're a software engineer, founder, business professional, marketer, designer, product manager, researcher, student, creator, educator, or community builder, your perspective is valuable. No prior hackathon experience is required—technical and non-technical participants are encouraged to collaborate and build together.
🤝 Connect with the AI Ecosystem
Meet and collaborate with AI founders, startups, enterprise leaders, investors, researchers, developer advocates, creators, educators, and industry experts.
The event creates opportunities to discover co-founders, teammates, mentors, customers, partners, investors, and future collaborators while becoming part of a growing AI innovation community.
Innovation Tracks
Participants are challenged to build an AI-native company, organization, or business function powered by a team of specialized AI employees.
Your solution should go beyond a single chatbot or AI agent. Think of it as building a digital workforce : multiple AI agents with distinct roles that collaborate, make decisions, execute workflows, communicate with each other, and continuously operate the business.
🌍 Social Impact & Climate
Build AI solution that improve lives, strengthen communities, and create a more sustainable future.
Examples : Climate & Sustainability, Environmental Protection, Social Impact, Disaster Response, Agriculture, Smart Cities, Non-profit Solutions, Community Engagement
❤️ Health & Wellness
Build AI solutions that improve healthcare, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples : Healthcare, Mental Health, Fitness, Nutrition, Elder Care, Wellness Platforms
🎓 Learning, Education & Research
Build AI solutions that transform education, research, and lifelong learning.
Examples : Schools & Universities, Personalized Learning, Tutoring, Professional Training, Research Assistants, Language Learning, Career Development, Knowledge Sharing
📈 Growth, Marketing & Go-to-Market (GTM)
Build AI solutions that help organizations grow, engage customers, and scale their businesses.
Examples : Marketing Automation, Sales Enablement, Customer Success, Branding, CRM, Customer Engagement, GTM Strategy, Business Analytics
🎬 Media, Entertainment & Creator Economy
Build AI solutions that redefine storytelling, creativity, and digital experiences.
Examples : Film Production, Music, Gaming, Streaming, Content Creation, Creator Tools, Social Media, Podcasts, Interactive Experiences
🛍️ Retail & Commerce
Build AI solutions that transform retail experiences and modern commerce.
Examples : E-Commerce, Retail Operations, Customer Experience, Marketplaces, Inventory Management, Supply Chain, Logistics, Loyalty Programs, Personalized Shopping
Core AI Capabilities
Regardless of the chosen track, every project is encouraged to demonstrate one or more of the following AI capabilities.
🔍 Discover & Research
Gather information, search knowledge sources, validate ideas, analyze trends, and generate insights.
🧠 Reason & Plan
Use AI for reasoning, planning, decision-making, strategy, and problem solving.
🤖 Multi-Agent Collaboration
Coordinate multiple AI agents that communicate, delegate tasks, collaborate, and execute complex workflows.
🎨 Create & Build
Generate websites, mobile applications, user interfaces, content, media, documents, and digital experiences.
🧠 Knowledge & Memory
Leverage long-term memory, knowledge bases, retrieval systems, contextual understanding, and organizational knowledge.
☁️ Compute & Intelligence
Utilize cloud infrastructure, AI models, inference, scalable compute, and high-performance AI workloads.
🛡️ Security & Trust
Design secure, reliable, privacy-aware, and responsible AI solutions with proper governance and authentication.
🚀 Deploy & Deliver
Deploy production-ready applications, integrate services, monitor performance, and deliver solutions that users can immediately experience.
Vision
The Universal Celebration Hackathon celebrates how AI can empower every individual—whether entrepreneur, student, creator, researcher, educator, healthcare professional, or business leader—to transform ideas into meaningful, real-world solutions.
By combining AI research, intelligent agents, rapid development, cloud infrastructure, and human creativity, participants will demonstrate how the next generation of AI-native applications can solve global challenges, accelerate innovation, and create lasting impact across every industry.
💡 Why Join?
The Universal Celebration Hackathon is more than a competition—it's an opportunity to build impactful AI solutions, explore ideas across diverse innovation tracks, learn from experienced mentors, and showcase your work to the community.
Whether your goal is to launch a startup, solve real-world challenges, grow your professional network, or accelerate your AI journey, you'll leave with valuable experience, meaningful connections, and opportunities that extend far beyond the event.
🎉 Build. Connect. Celebrate.
The future of AI won't be built by developers alone—it will be shaped by builders, founders, designers, business leaders, creators, researchers, investors, and communities working together.
Join hundreds of innovators for a day of building, learning, networking, and celebrating the incredible possibilities of AI.
Build bold ideas. Meet extraordinary people. Celebrate the future of AI.

Never written a line of code? Good. It’s time for non-technical people to join the hackathon—and become builders in one afternoon.
On September 4, Builder Pub is bringing the first-ever Non-Tech Buildathon to AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco .
We’ll begin with a short, hands-on introduction showing you how to use AI to build a working tool from scratch. Then, bring your own idea, join someone else’s, or form a team on the spot—and spend the afternoon turning an idea into something you can demo.
You don’t need coding experience, AI experience, a team, or even an idea before you arrive. We’ll help you find a place to start and stay nearby whenever you get stuck.

Please register through the AWS Builder Loft Portal: http://events.builder.aws.com/d/hcz0qt (Required by AWS)

This event is for designers, marketers, founders, operators, creators, students, and anyone who has ever thought:
“I have an idea, but I don’t know how to build it.”

“Hackathons sound exciting, but I’m not technical.”

“I want to build with AI, but I don’t know where to begin.”

How It Works
You can pitch an idea, join a project that sounds exciting, form a team with people you meet, or build independently.
Your project could be a useful personal tool, small web app, AI assistant, game, interactive experience, or something completely unexpected.
You bring the problem, the taste, and the decisions. AI helps with the technical implementation.
We’ll end with a community showcase, where teams and solo builders can demo what they created. Expect ambitious ideas, imperfect prototypes, last-minute fixes, and a few fun awards.

A working project or prototype

Join TrueFoundry and HackerSquad for a full-day Agent Harness hackathon focused on building production-minded agentic applications. The goal is simple: take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something that can be observed, governed, evaluated, and operated.

Guardrails need to become runtime controls: clear rules for what data an agent can see, which tools it can call, which actions require human approval, and how unsafe requests or outputs get blocked, logged, or escalated.

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed. That's harder to fake than a deck.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a road test. A hackathon judges what you built by the end. A road test watches how you handle the car.
The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

About Event

A twice-monthly working night for people building embodied AI. No robot required.
You built the arm at your kitchen table. You trained the policy overnight on your gaming rig. You collected the teleop data in your garage. The one thing none of it came with: labmates.
Degrees of Freedom is a monthly working night at Mission Robotics for everyone building physical AI without a lab around them. Bring the robot. Bring the sim that refuses to transfer. Bring the gripper that's been 80% assembled since the hackathon. For two hours, the people at the next bench are your labmates.

The person next to you has probably already hit your bug. Robotics failure is multidisciplinary: the fix is rarely in the field you know best. A room of mixed builders is the fastest debugger in the city.

A stated goal and two protected hours move a project further than most weekends do.

A robotics space with a test area and workshop, open on a Tuesday night. The best place in San Francisco to set a robot on a table and work.

About Event

For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending.

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers.
A tracker you never charge.
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco.

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen.

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.

Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.

AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.

Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.

What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream.

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.

Welcome to Founders & Friends third rooftop tech mixer of the season!
Join our monthly gathering for SF’s most ambitious founders, investors, tech professionals — and everyone in their orbit.
What is this?
200 of SF's most ambitious founders, operators, and investors. Sunset views. Real conversations.
Where?
We're taking over the beautiful 16 story luxury high-rise rooftop in SoMa. Details given to registered guests.
Who's coming?
Seasoned founders, investors, and operators — alongside the people still working up the nerve to start. Ambitious students with ideas, hackathon winners, creators, builders. The ones who haven't launched yet but probably should.
This is a space where the gap between "I have an idea" and "I'm building a company" gets a lot smaller. Other industries welcome too.
Come to fundraise. Come to hire. Come to find your co-founder. Or just come to be around people who make you feel like what you're building is actually possible.
Meet the Organizer — Founders & Friends
Founders and Friends was born from a feeling most builders know too well.
You have an idea. A real one. You start working on it alone, hit a wall, and stop. Then months later, you watch someone else build it — someone with more resources, more connections, more proximity to the right people.
That's not a talent gap. That's an access gap.
Founders and Friends exists to close it.
We bring together people with ideas and people who have cracked the code — the students crushing hackathons, early stage founders, operators, creators, investors, and seasoned entrepreneurs — in the same room, creating the kind of collisions that open doors and change trajectories.
Curated experiences designed to spark relationships between people who can move each other forward.
Because the best ideas don't die from lack of talent.
They die from lack of proximity.
We're building the community we all wish we had.
Meet the Organizer — Founder Social Club
Founder Social Club is a curated community designed to eliminate the loneliness of building a startup by bringing founders together through meaningful, high-quality connections. It combines intimate in-person gatherings, curated dinners, and virtual sessions with founders, investors, and operators—creating a space for honest conversations, shared experiences, and real relationships.
Focused on depth over scale, it offers founders access to peer support, insider knowledge, and a trusted network that grows alongside them.

Designli is the one-stop shop for SaaS founders looking to build and take their product to market efficiently. Whether you’re starting with an idea or scaling a platform with early traction, we make sure your software is scalable and secure, and that the go-to-market channels you build drive sustainable, continuous growth.

Finix
Finix is a full-stack payments infrastructure company that helps businesses accept payments, embed payments into their products, and send payouts at scale. Built on direct connections to Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover, Finix gives companies of all types the infrastructure to process, embed, and pay out through one API and dashboard.

ZUUZ is an AI that captures the deals hiding in your inbox. Built by a founder who found $740K of unlogged pipeline sitting in email, it auto-writes your CRM from real conversations, not manual entry
